The biggest myth about AI automation? That it takes months to get running. It shouldn’t.

A chatbot, voice agent or automated workflow doesn’t need a digital transformation project to go live. It needs a clear starting point (what is it answering, what is it booking) and a short build-and-test period, usually weeks, not months.

Your team doesn’t need training on new software either. The automation sits quietly in the background, doing the repetitive work, while your existing systems and processes carry on as normal.

If a solution needs six months before it’s worth anything, that’s a sign it’s the wrong solution, not a normal part of adopting AI.

Twelve tabs open. One piece of client work.

The document is in one place and the email about it is in another. Together, it's friction fatigue: the slow drain of switching tabs, re-entering data and chasing work that should already be filed.

Most firms don't have a technology problem. They have a fragmentation problem.

Our guide, Breaking Free From Friction Fatigue with Intelligent Workspaces, looks at where that friction builds up in professional service firms. One patient, two charts. It happens more often than most clinics think, and it causes real trouble.

A duplicate chart splits a patient's history in half: allergies in one record, last week's note in another, insurance on a third. Claims get confused, and the provider may not see the full picture.

A simple front-desk habit prevents most of it:
• Search by name and date of birth before creating anyone new
• Check spelling variations, hyphenated names and nicknames
• Confirm the date of birth with the patient, not just the form
• When in doubt, ask a teammate before adding a new record

In IKON EMR, the search-first step is built into patient demographics, so your team finds the existing chart before a duplicate ever gets started. Clean records start at check-in.
